docs.title: Never let a call's follow-ups fall through.
docs.text:
When a sales or customer call ends, the transcript is read automatically — the summary, every action item, and anything risky that came up (budget pushback, a competitor mention) land in your CRM sheet in seconds, and the owner is told immediately. A weekly digest catches any action item still open.

Reads the transcript from

Zoom Google Meet Google Calendar + Teams, Fireflies, Otter, or your transcript source

Tells the owner, wherever they already talk

WhatsApp Email Slack

Logs it wherever you already track deals

HubSpot Salesforce Google Sheets + Notion, Pipedrive, or yours Call ends transcript becomes available → RecapRelay reads it summary, action items, risks → Owner told in seconds Slack, WhatsApp, or email → Logged automatically deal recap + action items

Every Monday: a digest of every action item still open, oldest first.

A 2026 Salesforce survey of 4,050 sales professionals found reps spend only 40% of their week actually selling — the rest is admin, data entry, and internal meetings. A separate 2026 field-sales survey found 65% of reps spend 5+ hours a week on manual CRM entry alone.

docs.title: The problem this solves
docs.text:
The moment a call ends is when the deal is most alive in your head — and exactly then, writing it up competes with the next call, the next email, the rest of the day. So it waits. And once it waits, pieces of it start to go:

  • What was actually said gets thinner with every hour that passes, until "update the CRM" becomes a rushed two-line note days later, if it happens at all.
  • A commitment made out loud mid-call — "I'll send that by Friday," "let's reconnect Monday" — has nothing forcing it to become a tracked task once the call ends; it just lives in someone's memory until it doesn't.
  • A risk signal mentioned in passing — budget pushback, a competitor's name, a timeline slipping — vanishes along with the call itself unless someone happens to flag it.

RecapRelay reads the transcript the moment it's available, writes the recap and every action item to your sheet, and tells the owner immediately — so nothing depends on someone remembering to type it up later.

Curious how it actually works under the hood? See how it works · set it up.

Selling-time figure: Salesforce's 2026 State of Sales survey (4,050 sales professionals). Manual-entry figure: Spotio's 2026 field sales survey. Both are survey-based, not controlled studies — treat as directional.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text: This page goes deep on purpose — it's the proof that the homepage summary is real and tested, not just copy. You don't need to follow all of it to use the result.

docs.title: The flow
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  W[Call ends<br/>transcript ready] -->|webhook + secret| AI[Extract with AI]
  AI --> P[Parse AI response]
  P --> S[Read Settings]
  P --> E[Read existing meeting]
  P --> I[Read existing items]
  S --> B[Build Recap]
  E --> B
  I --> B
  B --> M[Meetings sheet<br/>add or update]
  M --> C1{Owner contact?}
  C1 -->|yes| N1[WhatsApp + email to owner]
  M --> BI[Build Action Items]
  BI --> AQ[Action Items sheet<br/>add or update]
  MON[Every Monday] --> RA[Read Action Items] --> RS[Read Settings] --> DG[Build digest] --> N2[WhatsApp + email to each owner]

All the business rules live in one file, recap.js. build.js copies it into the workflow's Code nodes, so the rules that are tested are the same ones that run. The AI step only reads the free-text transcript for the summary, action items, and risks — the account, contact, rep, and team come straight from the calendar/CRM metadata your intake system already has, never from the AI's guess.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text:
A row is always written, flagged or not, so nothing silently disappears:

Flag Meaning Missing: account/deal name, meeting summary The intake payload or the AI's extraction didn't return a required field No action items captured The AI didn't find anything actionable in the transcript — worth a glance, not necessarily wrong Risk flagged: ... The AI noticed something worth attention: budget pushback, a competitor mention, a slipping timeline No owner set for team ... Nobody in Settings to alert for that team

docs.title: When the same meeting comes in again
docs.text:
The workflow matches on the meeting ID (from Zoom, Google Meet, or whatever your calendar/transcript source provides).

  • The Meetings row updates in place rather than duplicating, keeping the original logged time.
  • Each action item's Status is never overwritten. This is the opposite rule from how SnapTally treats a changed invoice total, and deliberately so: here, a human marking an item Done is tracking real-world progress that has nothing to do with whether the transcript gets re-processed, so a corrected re-run only refreshes an item's text — never undoes someone's checkmark.

docs.title: Weekly digest
docs.text:
• Who it covers: every action item across every meeting that isn't marked Done.
  • What counts as stale: open 7 or more days.
  • Who's at the top: the five open items waiting longest, oldest first.

It goes to every owner listed in Settings, as a nudge for anything that's gone quiet.

docs.title: What's real and what's sample
docs.text:
• Real: the workflow, the rules, and their tests (node recap.test.js).
  • Sample:
  • send-test.sh posts one invented sample transcript with invented account/contact details.
  • The metadata fields in fromExtraction() (account, contact, rep, team) are a starting point — they assume your calendar or CRM already attaches this to the transcript webhook, which varies per client.
  • WhatsApp replies need a Meta-approved message template before the business can message a new contact first — that's Meta's rule, not a limitation of this workflow.

docs.text: File What recap.js All rules: normalizing the AI's output, flags, the recap row, action-item tracking, the weekly digest recap.test.js Fixed-input checks for every rule (node recap.test.js) build.js Builds workflow.json with recap.js inlined into the Code nodes workflow.json Import into n8n (no credentials inside) payloads/, send-test.sh A sample meeting payload and the script that sends it

docs.title: Set it up
docs.text:
You won't run any of this yourself if you hire me for it — this page is here so you (or your own dev team) can see exactly what's involved, and so there's a clean reference when I set it up for your account.

You need Docker and Node 18+, plus an Anthropic API key. Node is only used for the tests and build.js; n8n itself runs in Docker.

docs.title: 1. Run n8n locally
docs.text:
docker run -d --name n8n -p 5678:5678 -e GENERIC_TIMEZONE=Asia/Kolkata -e TZ=Asia/Kolkata -v n8n_data:/home/node/.n8n -v "$PWD:/files" docker.n8n.io/n8nio/n8n

Open http://localhost:5678 and create your login.

docs.title: 2. Google Sheet
docs.text:
Create a Sheet with three tabs:

Meetings — row 1 headers: 

Logged at, Meeting ID, Account, Contact, Team, Summary, Action items, Next step, Owner, Flags

Action Items — row 1 headers: 

Item ID, Meeting ID, Account, Item, Owner, Logged at, Status
Give Status a dropdown: Open, Done.

Settings — same sheet/pattern as CloseLoop and FirstReply, row 1 headers: 

Role, Team, Name, WhatsApp, Email
One row per team with Role = Team Owner, plus one Role = Fallback Owner row for anything unmatched.

Format every Logged at column as plain text (Format → Number → Plain text).

docs.title: 3. Credentials in n8n
docs.text:
• Anthropic API: add your API key as an HTTP Header Auth credential (header x-api-key), used by the Extract with AI node.
  • Google Sheets OAuth2 and Gmail OAuth2 (one OAuth client covers both; enable the Sheets, Drive and Gmail APIs): create an OAuth client in Google Cloud with redirect URI http://localhost:5678/rest/oauth2-credential/callback, then add the credential in n8n and sign in.
  • WhatsApp Business Cloud API: add your access token credential. Sends are wired but need an approved message template and billing enabled on the Meta account to actually go out.
  • Webhook secret: create a Header Auth credential named Intake webhook secret, header name X-Intake-Secret, long random value. Copy .env.example to .env with the same value.

docs.title: 4. Build, import, publish
docs.text:
SHEET_ID=<sheet id> WA_PHONE_ID=<whatsapp phone number id> node build.js

docker exec n8n n8n import:workflow --input=/files/workflow.json && docker exec n8n n8n publish:workflow --id=recapRelayMeetings1 && docker restart n8n

Open the workflow and pick your credentials on the webhook node, the Anthropic HTTP node, both Google Sheets nodes, the Gmail nodes, and the WhatsApp nodes. Then publish.

docs.title: 5. Try it
docs.text:
./send-test.sh payloads/new-meeting.json

A row should appear in the Meetings sheet, two rows in Action Items, and a recap email should arrive. Mark one action item Done, then send the same payload again — the Done status should survive.

To run the rule tests (no transcript or API key needed, since these feed the logic layer directly): node recap.test.js should print recap ok.

docs.title: Going live with a real transcript source
docs.text:
This is the one piece that's genuinely per-client, since "how does a transcript reach this workflow" varies:

  • Zoom: a webhook on the recording.transcript_completed event, with a step that pulls the transcript text and attaches the account/contact/rep/team your CRM or calendar already has for that meeting.
  • Google Meet / Teams: usually via a transcription add-on (Fireflies, Otter, or the platform's own transcript) posting to this same webhook once a transcript is ready.
  • Any other source: whatever gets you a transcript string plus the meeting's identifying metadata is enough — everything downstream of Extract with AI is already built and tested.
